script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Comedy
Theme: second chances

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. CAFETERIA - DAY

MIRA (mid-30s, overweight, disheveled, and wearing a faded lab coat) sits alone at a table, eating a sandwich. Across the room, JAMES (early 40s, average build, and wearing a suit) makes a presentation to a group of employees.

JAMES
(looking around the room)
And that's how, in just one year, we've managed to increase profits by 30%. Now, I know there's been some resistance to change, but I believe in all of you. You're all talented individuals, and I have faith that you can help take this company to new heights.

Mira looks up from her sandwich and rolls her eyes.

MIRA
(muttering to herself)
I'd love to see what he'd say if he knew I was the one who came up with the idea for the new product line.

The room empties, and James approaches Mira's table.

JAMES
Mira, I saw you there, taking notes. I take it you have some ideas?

Mira looks up at James, surprised.

MIRA
You noticed? I thought I was being discreet.

James smiles.

JAMES
I have a good memory for faces, and I remember yours from the marketing department. I always thought you had a lot of potential.

Mira looks skeptical.

MIRA
You think so? I was let go from marketing after the last product launch failed.

James looks sympathetic.

JAMES
I'm sorry about that. But I believe in second chances. I think it's time for you to come back and put your talents to good use.

Mira hesitates, then nods.

MIRA
Fine. I'll give it another try.

EXT. PARK - DAY

Mira and James walk through the park, talking about her new role in the company.

MIRA
I don't know if I can do it, James. I've been out of the industry for so long.

JAMES
You'll be fine. And if you need any help, I'll be there for you.

They reach a bench, and James sits down, patting the seat next to him. Mira sits down, looking at him doubtfully.

MIRA
How do you always manage to be so positive? It's impressive.

James smiles.

JAMES
I've had my fair share of failures in the past. But I've learned that every failure is just an opportunity to learn and grow.

Mira looks thoughtful.

MIRA
I suppose you're right. But I can't help feeling like I've blown my chance at a successful career.

James puts a comforting hand on her shoulder.

JAMES
Believe me, Mira, it's never too late to start over. You have all the skills and knowledge you need to succeed. All you have to do is believe in yourself.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - NIGHT

Mira sits at a table, scrolling through her phone. James enters and sits down across from her.

JAMES
Still working on that presentation?

Mira looks up, embarrassed.

MIRA
Yeah, I've been having a hard time getting started.

James leans back in his chair.

JAMES
Well, I have an idea that might help.

Mira looks at him hopefully.

JAMES
Why not focus on something you're passionate about? Something that excites you?

Mira thinks for a moment.

MIRA
I used to love creating recipes. Maybe I could come up with a new product line based on unique and delicious foods.

James smiles.

JAMES
That's the spirit! I have faith that you'll knock it out of the park.

INT. OFFICE - DAY

Mira presents her idea to James and the team. They're all impressed, and they begin brainstorming ways to make it a reality.

MIRA
This is it, James. This is my chance to prove myself.

James nods, looking proud.

JAMES
You've got this, Mira.

FADE OUT.

THE END
